\subsubsection{Scope of these measurements}\label{sss:dacr2r12-scope}

All data in this section is schematic-level. Layout and \texttt{av\_extracted} views
exist for both cells and have not been simulated, so no number here carries interconnect
parasitics --- which matter for an R-2R ladder, whose accuracy is a ratio of resistances
that layout can degrade.

\textbf{Settling time and glitch impulse were not measured.} The code bus is driven by a
\texttt{busset12} model that holds a static code, so every measurement in this section is
a sequence of DC solves. Code-step transients, and with them settling time, glitch
impulse and the major-carry glitch that an R-2R is prone to, require a different
stimulus and are not characterised.

\textbf{No settling or overshoot figure of merit is quoted for the supply block.} The
corner run's startup transient is valid and is plotted in
Figure~\ref{fig:dacr2r12-psu-startup}: \texttt{VddDac} reaches its zero-load DC value to
within \SI{140}{\micro\volt} at every corner and holds it. What cannot be published from
it is a number, because the bench's \texttt{t\_win} variable sets both the \texttt{En}
pulse width and the \texttt{settlingTime} evaluation window, so the two cannot be
specified independently. The Monte Carlo run of the same test is separately unusable: its
enable pulse is delayed \SI{1}{\second} against a \SI{500}{\micro\second} window, so
\texttt{En} never asserts and every startup output it reports grades the disabled state.
Note from the figure that the reference is pulled to the full \SI{2.5}{\volt} supply rail
for \SIrange{64}{100}{\nano\second} at the enable edge; any code held through an enable
event sees that excursion.

\textbf{Disabled-state supply current was not measured in this run.} The enable bench is
not part of the corner or Monte Carlo runs reported here. The last measurement of it,
\SI{59.45}{\micro\ampere} against a \SI{1}{\micro\ampere} target, comes from a superseded
setup and is not quoted as a result; it is a separate finding from the reference problem
of Section~\ref{sss:dacr2r12-supply} and needs re-measuring.

Which supply the ladder was referenced to is stated on every table and figure: the
\texttt{DacTB} results are against an ideal \SI{2.5}{\volt} rail and characterise the
ladder, and the \texttt{DacWPSUTB} results are against \texttt{VddDac} and characterise
the block as delivered. The corner run carries no mismatch information and the Monte
Carlo run varies process and mismatch together; the two are different quantities and are
never totalled.
